**July 4, 2026

** This year, we celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, whose main author was Thomas Jefferson.

But some Americans do not believe America is great and see little reason to celebrate. They believe our country was built on racism, slavery and sexism. But what they do not realize is that they are free to say this without the fear of arrest, imprisonment or even worse, ironically proving that America is great.
> We Americans love to celebrate our diversity. We have Columbus Day, St. Patrick's Day and Martin Luther King Day. Various ethnic groups have parades to honor their culture; and this is fine. But we often forget about the one group to whom we owe our freedom and prosperity - the Anglo-Saxons.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2f01fbf-ea79-4cfe-bbac-ca390638aedf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
King Charles III
> Tenth century England was a primitive place. It was barely an Iron Age culture, with marauding tribes engaged in internecine struggles among themselves and against the invading Vikings. Illiteracy was the norm. Meanwhile, Japan had established an advanced culture of writing and literature. Thirteenth century China built ships ten times the size of those Columbus used to cross the Atlantic. The Arab world invented algebra, advanced architecture and a body of literature that delights children to this day. Meanwhile, the English survived by subsistence farming, lived in huts and walked around in clothing that was nothing more than a burlap sack. Yet the people from this small island established global hegemony. Why? Because while other cultures lived under Rule of Men, the English developed Rule of Law.
> Ever since King John was forced to sign the Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215, the English people chipped away at privilege and power, enabling all citizens to be equal in the eyes of the Law. The Magna Carta allowed heirs to inherit property without confiscation by the State. It ended the practice of forcing wealthy widows to marry politically connected nobility and merchants. Parliament was eventually established. The much maligned Richard III promulgated the concept of a free press and bail for the accused. [The Petition of Right in 1628](https://substack.com/redirect/702bac97-1031-4c7d-9e4f-eb55ac9cefdd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) prohibited excessive taxation and the quartering of soldiers in one's house. It created the concept of habeas corpus - meaning you could not be arrested without being accused of a crime. The English fought for the right to bear arms, worship freely and not have to pay damages for a crime one did not commit. These became known as the Rights of Englishmen and when King George III refused to extend these rights to the American colonies, our forefathers rebelled.
> It has become fashionable among our cultural elite to disparage our forefathers as racists, homophobes, misogynists and elitists. But they were great men. The entire planet dreams of living in England or one of its children - whether it be the United States, Canada, Australia or New Zealand. Iran does not have an illegal immigration problem.
> So this Fourth of July, permit me to raise a glass of cognac to the man who sailed to Sicily and convinced my grandfather and my great uncles to immigrate to the United States and work in the coal mines of Pennsylvania. My grandfather despised this man, disparaging him with the term "Johnny Bull." He felt he had been deceived as this life-threatening, back breaking work paid poorly. But when my grandfather made money, he got to keep it. And when he built a house for my grandmother, my father and his five siblings; no Mafia thug could take it away from him. And his children became college professors. And his grandchildren became doctors and lawyers. And his great grandchildren went to fine universities and live a life style and have opportunities my grandfather could never have conceived.
> So I hope the descendants of this man are as fat and happy as we are; and I hope that at some time in my career, one of his descendants came into my office, shook my hand and thanked me when I handled his eye problem competently.
>

# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=7537%2E582294%2EA1SHc4)
I joined Jen Psaki tonight to talk about why New Hampshire is shaping up to be one of the most important Senate races in the country.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260703_2.um_0Tv&refcode=em20260703-2&t=2&akid=7537%2E582294%2EA1SHc4)
**The fight for the Senate majority could come down to what happens right here in the Granite State.**
Republicans know this race is one of their best opportunities to flip a seat. That's why they're already pouring millions into New Hampshire and planning to spend millions more.
We can win this race – but only if we keep building the kind of grassroots campaign that has powered us from the very beginning.
After my conversation with Jen on the stakes of this race, I need to ask: **[Can you chip in $25, or whatever you can, to help us keep this momentum going and show that New Hampshire is ready for this fight?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260703_2.um_0Tv&refcode=em20260703-2&t=3&akid=7537%2E582294%2EA1SHc4)**

I've spent my career fighting to lower costs for working families, protect our fundamental freedoms, and make government work for the people it's supposed to serve – not the wealthy and well-connected.
That's what's at stake in this election.
The national attention on our race is only going to grow from here, and the attacks and outside spending will grow right alongside it. We need to be prepared for everything that's coming.
**[If you're with me, please make a contribution of $25 or whatever you can to my campaign today.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260703_2.um_0Tv&refcode=em20260703-2&t=23&akid=7537%2E582294%2EA1SHc4)**

name: Susan Collins
subject: Happy 250th Birthday, America! 🇺🇸
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Collins for Senator
body:
May we continue to stand strong and united.

|
---
Peter, Today, we celebrate an extraordinary milestone in our nation's history: the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States of America.Two and a half centuries ago, our Founders embarked on a bold experiment in self-government founded on the enduring principles of liberty, equality, and opportunity. Through times of triumph and challenge alike, generations of Americans have worked to preserve those ideals and strengthen our democracy.From the rocky coast of Maine to communities across our great nation, Americans have always shown remarkable resilience, generosity, and determination. Our differences have never diminished our shared commitment to freedom, opportunity, and the promise that hard work and perseverance can build a better future.It is the honor of my lifetime to represent the people of Maine in the United States Senate. Every day, I am inspired by the independence, kindness, and strength of Mainers, and I remain committed to working on their behalf and helping to ensure that our state and our nation continue to thrive.As we gather with family, friends, and neighbors this Independence Day, let us celebrate all that unites us, reflect on the sacrifices made by those who came before us, and look ahead with confidence and hope.Happy 250th Birthday, America. May God continue to bless our great nation.Warmly,Susan CollinsU.S. Senator for Maine

# Saturday, July 4, 2026

**Happy Fourth of July!** On this day in 1776, the Continental Congress formally adopted the Declaration of Independence, announcing the American colonies' separation from Great Britain and [giving birth to a new nation](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOqzAQgOHTmC5oPHYAFy5eQ5fXbokcPISJHIzs2SBuv8peYetf-or_6zbdAifeHv_Di7wsedroqIlEqEy8Rdppi7TNFMO5UpB7ClXKhIDdBfoL2CkGTudkm-gXIiTTkNf9YPTVDQaa1QORQ3SddQtZMLOJYKzuEOcruHi_N-w_GvRgNWjAvtV26LULA0WDiw5OWaDIkkv7zLzJSks685tKO-dXk_wqsldl_ikcFY7HcbQrV8nl_HSFYyjCc6KqcHx-p_NiZW2Kj_vBKXHtemXh8Qqcfjn504O3x58AAAD__w6Gb7g).

As our nation commemorates its 250th birthday this weekend, we'll be sending out shortened editions through Monday so _The Flyover _staff can celebrate the holiday with friends and family. Our regular edition will return on Tuesday. Have a safe and happy Fourth of July weekend! Are you the one setting off fireworks, or the one lying awake wishing they'd stop? Somewhere on your street tonight, someone's going till midnight while the dog shakes under the bed and half the block wonders if they're the only ones who've had enough. Fireworks are the sound of the Fourth, the whole country looking up at once. But they're also sparking wildfire fears, veterans bracing at every crack, and thousands of ER visits a year. So are they worth it? Tune in to today's _Flyover Podcast_ as Amy shares both sides of the story. Which side are you on? [Tune in here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzzFuwyAUgOHTmC0WPFPAA0OXbOnaET38nmMqAhZGSX37qr1CD_D_0vd5CzdMOZX7Bz7Y97WGwq8jc-_cQirEOxfisjDhuTH2mPHoLYAEc5H2InUgTPkMWpBfmYEnwV5ZN6m32U1SbN4QWONc5BgjxWVmNAA64hLlCoZQJP97k1ZqJZUEOyrtrJrRMU2wKpwHLZlSr238qqn0jdd81ie3cakPkf3W-34M0_sA1wGujWPDQmM-B7julfi7N1SiedpfKed0GDtoeX9gyn99_xf66eEnAAD__8vWa7c)!****

We're always interested in products that take an everyday task and simply make it easier. ## Heat Wave Blasts July 4 Celebration Plans
A dangerous heat wave pushing temperatures past 100 degrees across the Northeast has forced dozens of 250th-anniversary events [to be canceled, postponed, or moved indoors](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAQRk-DOyIYQ7ALim3cZdstLdYM8UQYLDxJ5NuvvFf46096n97785gfgTKV5--woedU54LfIyMztplKxB1LxLJgDOeKgf_mcHCbQcFdKieVmWOgfM6miz4hAvYdeu2GXttx6FW3ensfB-VG1EH3Fq2JKUGySRsDo9EpdeQvmnLKaKUVuJs2g9NjGDD2kHQYhVEYiWu7vSoVXjHls36w3Za6ddmvzPsh-l8CJgETr7hSztcmYFrrhpeQgCnEjQod3AJTLQImO1oAN8jUEGPdJFglub23Xb7e-ZRGXr5yqWXBVi5C13zcv5QzHXcnjHpugf4fdfyjch8P_wIAAP__BZeBmg). On the National Mall in Washington, D.C., organizers kept the Great American State Fair open while adding hydration stations, misting fans, and climate-controlled tents.

The National Weather Service [forecasts highs of 102 or above in Washington on July 4,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u6yAUAOCnwVusw0-CGRiuEnnLXSt1sQ7mENMSQBglSp--al-hL_AN39t1uWJMMd_-451sD2XJ9NwT9U5tidlTpewpr-TxtRF2l3DvbREgTgfQB1CLx5heixq8DUSC5ECW60nyo5kkDJtVRgvhtKaTVs4Fg6s_SjDoJjM54cIQ7Y8GGhQHDkKPXE2aG5zISxE4GqaAfOyljR8l5r5RSK_yoDau5T4ku_Vedyb_MTEzMYfSaMW9j0_CvlEbb-XBxHzFek5x_RzrVpmcv0qm6Jm8XM7vAHxo1tdnTCnuJ80U3O4Y0y_f_3TysOI7AAD__2ZadPc) with heat index values pushing well past 110, after Washington, New York, and Boston all hit 100 on Thursday. Entry to the National Mall for today's "Salute to America" fireworks has been pushed back to 5 p.m. to limit heat exposure. Elsewhere in the Northeast, parades in Norristown, Pa., and Haddon Township, N.J., were scrapped over safety concerns, Philadelphia canceled its Salute to Independence Semiquincentennial Parade outright Friday morning, and Gettysburg National Military Park moved all outdoor activities indoors. [See the full list of changes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1utDAURVcDnZHfs_krXHzNdPO1KdELvgxOjEFggWb3EdlC-qN7dc7Hc3hKiCG9_ssCl6d1SLiOiJyxDyF5bEgeaYSX9wzJn1GOvA-suVG6VdoOXkJ8D7b0bgIYpoSjtjNU953R5ey8wWil4cmQmdhSf0MNGWk8d0S2DO5e0622pElzW5HtWuqlgzc8kfSF1fAhr3v1tYaUZ0zxvZ7Yq3FdyujmnLejMP8KfhT8uK6ruhUu4PsGCn7EcGQlC_YwiuJaK5xI-VCjpBERXu3YoqQEr25FdckJRUy1rjtb7s5vV4gxHE1bWP1aJMTf5_ynXKfjnwAAAP__yMN-DA) to events.
## Rare 'Declaration' Copy Found in London
A volunteer at Britain's National Archives has discovered a [rare 1776 printing](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGvpSAUhH8NdhhAvUhBsY3d3XZLc4TD9exywSBX47_f-KrXv24yk0zmmz_P-QkUKb1-wxttDXlOeO4Ra8UyU_K4YfKYHHq4VoS6RNhrmZVQDy40F_3sgeI19423AVFh16CVeuzkYMZONKs18qEXufSD6YwCHKReQPtghPJucOPYkL3bhBa9FFIo3cp-1NLAiL5TQYJhvUBPNZf2b6ZUVwzxygeW1uV3E-1a67az7hdTE1PTeZ6tW_ab4s6Zmm7J1HRAon2l9IoXL1CQu7xdPAdeV-QeXYQClXK6re_gPORP8pwS__B_fLn4keMnVcTC1NQU67eTYqT9oVkvXm-g-LWr_ujMw6r_AQAA__-USIsf) of the Declaration of Independence, one of only 11 surviving "Exeter Declarations" and the only copy known outside the United States. The document was [seized on Christmas Eve 1776](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOiN7bQIULv6GLn97Jdp418F3jo2ME5S3P3HV9dfOSKP5vo_rcsUQQ7r_xwfb6vOS-Ngj18plCYl440ScHBO-V8Z6i7jXsoCEi5CDkGYhDPG9mJasZwbWLVs1jFr106hlu1pwdGOSGidPiJLYe_Ra6qm_GO96boM91-QgjZJKwtApMw5qwpFJg1c4NUYyhZpL95lDqiv7-M4vLp3LjzbatdZtb_S_BuYG5uM4unRzJ8XZn0kukRqY-Vnyxg3MBQsLYhexYA05id-cwudnIhGSeH6J4hLqHsYe2mJpO0KMYb8MjZH3B4b4c6D-ydrLwncAAAD__3bWgxM) when the Royal Navy captured the American privateer _Dalton_ off Portugal after a seven-hour chase. Logged simply as "another paper," it sat unnoticed for 250 years. "Exeter Declarations" are a specific batch of early printed copies of the Declaration of Independence, produced by printer Robert Luist Fowle in Exeter, New Hampshire, between July 16 and 19, 1776, roughly two weeks after the original was adopted in Philadelphia on July 4. Volunteer Michael Scurr found it while cataloguing Navy correspondence. It will go on display in the Archives' [Revolution 250 exhibition](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHznCAQRz8NdjiA-ucoKNLYXdqUzh4sSrIHDqLGb5_xqqRO-2bnzf7ej-f0hEgxzd_hjbaGPCU8N8JasUwxeVwxeUwOPVwLQn0RbLVMSqgvLjQX_eQh0jX1jbcBUWHXoJX60cnBPDrRLHboX3LQ2gwQOjNoOSjAlxTGKRmMML6J9rYJLXoppFC6lf1DSwMP9J0KEgzrBfpYc2l_5pjqgoGufGBpXX43ZJda141135gamRrP82wT1JgTEBS3xAO3ds5Hu_9iasTfK-WCvC7IXSZCd18yNf4L-IvyzNQYSn7zvBd-ZNpTRSzbTWPyMc0ceMKTu7xePIePct-4R0dQPg_c9O-ETI1NsX49I1HcvjTrxfyGSJ8d9b_iH1b9CQAA__9qGJzK), running through November.
